comment: The WASM parity matrix, as data, so the two sides cannot drift apart.
The whole point of the acceptance test is that both run the identical
sequence, and the cheapest way to guarantee that is one definition of it.
layouts: every one, including the TOWN and LANDSCAPE drawing layers --
the two most likely to expose a portability difference.
seeds: zero, a small odd one, and one with the high bit set, since the seed
is a byte and sign-extension is a classic cross-target difference.
frames: 9.6 simulated seconds, long enough that the world has cast and
landed rather than only sampling the opening frame.
tick_ms: SIM_TICK_MS, as duel_city_frame_interval_ms reports it.
semantic: cases that set host semantics instead of starting from a tour
stop, every field away from its default. The browser takes no input, so
the native and Swift legs run these and the WASM leg does not.
